leads.summary: New explanatory comment overstates what a failed stop stage establishes

This does not make the new stderr wrong, since it now avoids claiming either outcome; qualify the comment to avoid turning that inaccurate premise into a later status or cleanup decision.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** No new defects in `48d205c`; the restart-failure and assertion findings from the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13085#issuecomment-5854813553) are resolved, and the #13101 overlap remains in narrowed form.

- **Restart-failure message:** resolved, as the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13085#issuecomment-5879276130) states. Each tested failure path prints the neutral text and exits 1 after one sudo call.
- **Assertion that could not fail:** resolved. A keep-escalating mutant passes the `e1c1b1b` suite 10/10 and fails this one.
- **#13101 overlap:** still present, corrected to a narrower claim (Details).
- **#11936 / bt-agent:** unverified here. The author's log matches the named check for a clean restart.
- **New, related:** open PR #13668 also edits this script and adds a same-named test file; both conflict (Details).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:** sudo refused and a failed restart job both print the neutral message. The PR suite passes 10/10 at `48d205c` and on a merge with `quattro`. The added `sudo` logging changes no other assertion.

**Note, new related open PR:** #13668 also changes `bin/omarchy-restart-bluetooth` for #13078 and adds a same-named `test/shell.d/restart-bluetooth-test.sh`. Merging it with this head conflicts in both files.

**#13101 correction:** the previous review said any conflict resolution keeps #13101's unchecked restart lines. That is too strong: a resolver can delete them by hand. Picking this PR's side of both hunks does keep them. The bluetooth service then restarts twice per run, and this PR's suite fails at `restart bluetooth stops before btusb when the restart failed` (2 sudo calls). #13101's own test file still passes.

**Suggested change:** whichever PR lands second, delete #13101's unchecked restart lines when resolving the conflict, not only the marked hunks; this PR's suite catches a leftover restart.

**bt-agent:** #11936's reporter saw the opposite (same PID, no re-registration), which remains unexplained. Open issue #13247 describes a related outcome of the same sequence. bt-agent's replacement starts 2 s after it exits, and its `ExecCondition` checks that `bluetooth.service` is active. If `bluetooth.service` is not active again within those 2 s, the unit is skipped and not retried for that session, which is what #13247's journal shows. Not tested here. After the menu action, `systemctl --user show bt-agent -p Result -p ConditionResult` showing `Result=exec-condition` would confirm it.

**Optional notes:**
- The PR description says the denied-restart count "is 1 when the script stops there and 3 when it reaches the reload". With sudo refused, a script that goes on makes 2 calls: the refused `modprobe -r` skips the load. 3 applies only when sudo works. The test comment's "twice over" has the same imprecision.
- The failed-restart case asserts only the prefix `Could not restart bluetooth.service`, so restoring the old second sentence still passes 10/10. Matching `Check 'systemctl status bluetooth.service'` as well would pin it.
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: sudo count in the denied-restart case</summary>

# Reproducer: the PR description's sudo count for the denied-restart case

Status: PR description wording only (not a code defect). Reproduced at `48d205cfc9adb5a4a0ca46f1f1cf27884c356eb3`.

The PR description says the denied-restart case "asserts exactly one call — it is 1 when the script stops there and 3 when it reaches the reload". With sudo refused on every call (as that test case sets it up), a script that keeps escalating reaches `sudo modprobe -r btusb`. That call is also refused, so the `else` branch runs and `sudo modprobe btusb` is never attempted: the count is 2, not 3. The count is 3 only when sudo succeeds (the author's reply table labels that row correctly). The assertion `(( sudo_calls == 1 ))` still fails the mutant, so the test itself is sound.

## Script

Save as `repro-sudo-count.sh` and run `bash repro-sudo-count.sh <omarchy checkout at 48d205c>`. It uses the stubs from `test/shell.d/restart-bluetooth-test.sh` verbatim, the arguments of the case `restart bluetooth stops before btusb when the restart failed` (`never yes yes yes`), and a mutant in which the failed restart sets a flag instead of exiting and the script exits 1 only at the end.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Count the sudo calls the PR's denied-restart case sees for the pinned script
# and for a "keeps escalating" mutant of it (the failed restart no longer exits;
# the script exits 1 only at the end). Uses the PR test's own stubs.
# Usage: repro-sudo-count.sh <omarchy checkout at the PR head>
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1
tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_dir"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$tmp_dir/bin"

# Stubs copied from test/shell.d/restart-bluetooth-test.sh at 48d205c.
cat >"$tmp_dir/bin/rfkill" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'rfkill %s\n' "$*" >>"$STUB_CALLS"
STUB
cat >"$tmp_dir/bin/sudo" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'sudo %s\n' "$*" >>"$STUB_CALLS"
[[ $STUB_SUDO_FAILS == "yes" ]] && exit 1
exec "$@"
STUB
cat >"$tmp_dir/bin/systemctl" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'systemctl %s\n' "$*" >>"$STUB_CALLS"
if [[ $1 == "is-active" ]]; then
  [[ $STUB_DAEMON_ACTIVE == "yes" ]] && exit 0
  exit 3
fi
[[ $1 == "restart" && $STUB_CONTROLLER_AFTER == "restart" ]] && touch "$STUB_STATE/controller"
exit 0
STUB
cat >"$tmp_dir/bin/modprobe" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'modprobe %s\n' "$*" >>"$STUB_CALLS"
[[ $1 == "-r" && $STUB_UNLOAD_FAILS == "yes" ]] && exit 1
[[ $1 == "btusb" && $STUB_CONTROLLER_AFTER == "btusb" ]] && touch "$STUB_STATE/controller"
exit 0
STUB
cat >"$tmp_dir/bin/lsmod" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
[[ $STUB_BTUSB_LOADED == "yes" ]] && echo "btusb                  73728  0"
exit 0
STUB
cat >"$tmp_dir/bin/bluetoothctl" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'bluetoothctl %s\n' "$*" >>"$STUB_CALLS"
if [[ $1 == "list" && -f $STUB_STATE/controller ]]; then
  echo "Controller AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF omarchy [default]"
fi
exit 0
STUB
chmod +x "$tmp_dir"/bin/*

cp "$repo/bin/omarchy-restart-bluetooth" "$tmp_dir/pinned"
# Mutant: the failed restart sets a flag instead of exiting; exit 1 at the end.
sed -e '/^if ! sudo systemctl restart bluetooth.service; then$/,/^fi$/ s/^  exit 1$/  restart_failed=1/' \
  "$tmp_dir/pinned" >"$tmp_dir/mutant"
printf '\nif [[ -n ${restart_failed:-} ]]; then exit 1; fi\n' >>"$tmp_dir/mutant"
chmod +x "$tmp_dir/pinned" "$tmp_dir/mutant"
echo "mutant diff:"
diff "$tmp_dir/pinned" "$tmp_dir/mutant" || true

run() { # script sudo_fails
  rm -rf "$tmp_dir/state"; mkdir -p "$tmp_dir/state"; : >"$tmp_dir/calls"
  local rc=0
  STUB_STATE="$tmp_dir/state" STUB_CALLS="$tmp_dir/calls" STUB_CONTROLLER_AFTER=never \
    STUB_BTUSB_LOADED=yes STUB_DAEMON_ACTIVE=yes STUB_SUDO_FAILS="$2" STUB_UNLOAD_FAILS=no \
    OMARCHY_BLUETOOTH_RESTART_WAIT=1 OMARCHY_BLUETOOTH_RELOAD_WAIT=1 \
    PATH="$tmp_dir/bin:$PATH" "$tmp_dir/$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
  printf '%-7s sudo_fails=%-3s exit=%s sudo_calls=%s: %s\n' "$1" "$2" "$rc" \
    "$(grep -c '^sudo ' "$tmp_dir/calls" || true)" "$(grep '^sudo ' "$tmp_dir/calls" | paste -sd ';' -)"
}
run pinned yes
run mutant yes
run pinned no
run mutant no
```

## Actual output (sandboxed run, all six commands stubbed)

```text

---

pinned  sudo_fails=yes exit=1 sudo_calls=1: sudo systemctl restart bluetooth.service
mutant  sudo_fails=yes exit=1 sudo_calls=2: sudo systemctl restart bluetooth.service;sudo modprobe -r btusb
pinned  sudo_fails=no  exit=1 sudo_calls=3: sudo systemctl restart bluetooth.service;sudo modprobe -r btusb;sudo modprobe btusb
mutant  sudo_fails=no  exit=1 sudo_calls=3: sudo systemctl restart bluetooth.service;sudo modprobe -r btusb;sudo modprobe btusb
```

The `sudo_fails=yes` rows are the test case's arrangement: 1 call for the pinned script, 2 for the mutant. The `sudo_fails=no` rows show where 3 comes from. Suggested wording: "it is 1 when the script stops there and 2 when it goes on to the reload (the refused `modprobe -r` skips the load)".
